# App Worker errors reach no sink that does not require a Brain checkout

## Context

#18551 broke every Workstation viewport vdom sync and shipped with 24/24 CI green. @tobiu found it by opening the app in a browser. Investigating why nothing caught it turned up a cause underneath the missing assertions: **an App Worker error has nowhere to go that does not require a private Brain checkout.**

Split off #18554, which owns the test gate. That gate cannot be built until this channel exists, and this channel is worth having on its own.

## The Problem

A Neo app raises its errors in the App Worker. `src/worker/App.mjs:397` wraps `console[log|warn|error|info]` and `:445` hooks `globalThis.onerror`. **Both route exclusively to `Neo.ai?.Client`** — the Neural Link bridge. The wrapper does still call `original.apply(console, args)`, but in SharedWorker mode that writes to the SharedWorker's own inspector context, which the page never sees.

So an App Worker error is visible to exactly two audiences:

1. a developer who knows to open the SharedWorker's separate DevTools context, and
2. a Neural Link session, which needs `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` pointing at a `neo-agent-brain` checkout.

It is visible to nobody else — not the page console, not a browser-driving test, not a developer who simply has the app open. #18551 spent its whole life in that blind spot: the throw was caught by `VdomLifecycle.mjs:378` and logged, and the log went where only the Brain could read it.

**This is a channel gap, not a missing assertion.** No quantity of added test assertions can observe a signal that never arrives.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/worker/App.mjs:397` — `interceptConsole()`, the console wrapper. Sink: `Neo.ai?.Client` only.
- `src/worker/App.mjs:445` — `globalThis.onerror`. Sink: `Neo.ai?.Client` only.
- `src/Main.mjs` — the `remote.app` manifest **already exposes `log`**, and `Main.log(data)` is `console[data.method || 'log'](data.value)`. It has **zero callers** in the repository. The channel this ticket needs already exists and is dead code.
- `src/worker/mixin/RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:generateRemote` — every remote proxy returns `promiseMessage`, which rejects with `NEO_DEAD_PORT` when a window closed. A forward must swallow that.
- `src/worker/Base.mjs:450` — an unrouted `'main'` destination emits `console.warn` about its own deprecation under SharedWorker. That warning would arrive back through the interceptor doing the forwarding.

## The Fix

In `interceptConsole()`, mirror `error`-level output and the `onerror` payload to the main thread via the existing `Neo.Main.log`, addressed per connected window.

Nothing is added to any manifest and no new addon appears; the only new surface is one protected method plus a re-entrancy latch. Serialisation moves out of the Brain-client branch into `serializeConsoleArgs` so the mirror does not depend on a client being attached — that independence is the entire point.

Constraints the shape has to respect, each for a checked reason rather than a guessed one:

- **Errors only.** Volume with no consumer is noise, and `warn` is what the deprecated-destination path emits.
- **Never in production.** A diagnostic mirror, not a logging transport.
- **Addressed per `windowId`.** Avoids the deprecated unrouted `'main'`, whose warning would re-enter the interceptor.
- **Re-entrancy latched and rejections swallowed.** The mirror runs *inside* `console.error`; anything it logs comes back to it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 — an App Worker error reaches the page console.** Verified against a real defect, not a synthetic throw: with #18551's `syncTopologyBar` reinstated on a local branch, the Workstation boot produces `App Worker: … Component not found for id: neo-component-34` in the **page** console, with no Brain checkout and no Neural Link.
- [ ] **AC-2 — a healthy app mirrors nothing.** Absence control, in CI. Without it, AC-1 would be satisfied by a mirror that fired on everything, which is as useless as one that never fires.
- [ ] **AC-3 — level and environment are both bounded.** `log`/`warn`/`info` are not mirrored, and nothing is mirrored when `Neo.config.environment` is `dist/production`.
- [ ] **AC-4 — the mirror cannot become a fault of its own.** A dead port rejects without logging; a re-entrant call is latched out. Both are reachable states, not hypotheticals: `NEO_DEAD_PORT` is ordinary window teardown, and the unrouted-destination warning is one line away in `worker/Base.mjs`.
- [ ] **AC-5 — no new remote surface.** `git grep` shows the Main `remote.app` manifest unchanged; the forward uses the `log` entry that already existed with no callers.

## Out of Scope

- **The test gate that fails a spec on a mirrored error.** #18554 owns it, and it stays open. It is not bundled here because its own failure path cannot yet be exercised in CI: the App-Worker remote manifest exposes no way to provoke a worker error, and `destroyNeoInstance` correctly routes through `parent.remove()`, so no public path produces an orphan stub. Shipping a guard whose red path is unproven is the failure this whole thread is about.
- **`unhandledrejection`.** Not currently hooked by `interceptConsole` either, so mirroring it would be new coverage rather than a new path for existing coverage. Worth its own look; named here so it is not mistaken for an oversight.
- **The `'App Worker: '` prefix coupling.** The mirror writes it in the browser and #18554's gate would match it in Node; they cannot share an import. Guarding that pair belongs with the gate that depends on it.
- **Changing `VdomLifecycle.mjs:378`.** Logging rather than throwing is the documented intent.

## Avoided Traps

- **Adding a new remote method or a Main addon.** `Main.log` already had exactly this shape and no callers. Adding a second one would have been accretion on top of dead code.
- **Mirroring every level.** Turns the page console into a worker log tail and gives a future gate nothing it can assert on.
- **Attaching a CDP session to the `shared_worker` target from the harness instead.** No engine change, but Chromium-only harness plumbing that helps no human developer and leaves the underlying invisibility in place.

## Decision Record impact

`none`. Adds a development-only diagnostic path over an existing remote method; no runtime contract changes.
